paragraphs.text: At god's hour, bow to the Lord. Then be still, be restrained, do the twilight rite. Give two watches to chanting and honoring — the rest of the day is leftovers, and leftovers belong to Śiva.

First the alphabet stands up as a goddess: A for head, KA for hands, ṬA for feet, both sides for PĀ, the middle for ṂA, the heart for YA — all of it knowing-shaped. Her name is Sarasvatī, and she wins.
Thought-jewel, wish-cow, wish-tree: they fruit exactly what men wish for, no more, no less. Nobody asked, nothing piled up — so, noble Mother-mood, please grow what men are really after.
Nothing gets done without her, nothing is known, nothing is even wanted — she is the lady who owns all knowing. To the highest one, the mother of worlds — honor to Śivā, Śiva's own beloved.

She is always rising, always blessed, all good luck, giving Śiva, living in Śiva's heart — O Śivā. Moonlight that opens the night lotus: for a mind that worships, make my going the highest going there is.
Be kind, all-luck Śivā, Śiva's darling. Umā! Ramā! Sarasvatī! You, you alone, are the top goddess.
Mother! Formless Lady, nameless one! Umā, Angry One, Leftward One, Great Lakṣmī, Māyā! Goddess of the five-act play, lovely Bhairavī in all her glory — I am yours, I bow down.

Māyā, Learning, Mātṛkā, Garland-girl — you throb away in every single body as a spark of knowing. How am I supposed to sit with you, all flashing by yourself? I sit with you as the voice talking inside itself.
